entries.text: B1 Backup file name `spec.md` says `.bak.YYYY-MM-DD.HHMMSS`. `plan.md` says `FILE.YYYY-MM-DD.HHMMSS.bak`. a) `FILE.bak.YYYY-MM-DD.HHMMSS` (spec wording) b) `FILE.YYYY-MM-DD.HHMMSS.bak` (plan wording) (Recommended: it keeps the extension last, so editors and globs still find it) c) Something else
entries.answer: b) `FILE.YYYY-MM-DD.HHMMSS.bak` (plan wording) (Recommended: it keeps the extension last, so editors and globs still find it) Answered by kig on 2026-11-03

entries.text: B2 Does encrypt create backups? `spec.md` backs up the existing target on "No" for both directions. `plan.md` backs up only on decrypt, and encrypt overwrites without a backup. a) Backups for both encrypt and decrypt, as the spec says b) Backups for decrypt only, as the plan says (Recommended: the encrypted file is not plaintext, and a backup of it adds clutter)
entries.answer: b) Backups for decrypt only, as the plan says (Recommended: the encrypted file is not plaintext, and a backup of it adds clutter) Answered by kig on 2026-11-03

entries.text: B3 Is `-O` a short flag for `--overwrite`? `spec.md` gives `--overwrite` no short form. `plan.md` gives `-O`, which is easy to confuse with `-o`. a) `--overwrite` only, no short flag (Recommended) b) `-O` as in the plan
entries.answer: b) `-O` as in the plan Answered by kig on 2026-11-03

entries.text: B4 Scope of the change The spec wants the prompt rules also applied to `-o`, which changes today's silent overwrite behaviour. The plan adds `0600`/`0700` modes, an atomic temp-file rename and a git ignore warning. Each is a separate design choice. a) Keep all of it in one plan, as written b) Split: (1) `-w` naming and the target-exists rules, (2) file modes and atomic writes, (3) the git warning (Recommended) c) Move the plan to `starts: planning` and write the split there
entries.answer: b) Split: (1) `-w` naming and the target-exists rules, (2) file modes and atomic writes, (3) the git warning Answered by kig on 2026-11-03

entries.text: B2 Behaviour on a "No" answer at the overwrite prompt The plan's Existing target table says that on "No" a backup is created. D2 says only decrypt creates backups, and the spec says a backup is made before writing. It does not say whether a "No" answer still writes the new file. a) On "No", leave the target untouched and write nothing (Recommended) b) On "No", back up the target, then write the new file (the spec's literal reading)
entries.answer: b) On "No", back up the target, then write the new file (the spec's literal reading) Answered by kig on 2026-11-03
